extracted.intended_audience: advocates, stakeholders, or practitioners interested in submitting public comments to federal agencies (e.g., HUD)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing effective public comment letters to federal agencies during notice-and-comment rulemaking, including process, structure, legal assessment, and filing mechanics. Focused on practical tips for commenters to influence agency rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide provides an overview of how federal rulemaking works as context for where and how comments fit; described as part of the seven-page Brookings guide referenced by the post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a comment letter
rubrics_metrics.description: How to structure a comment letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide includes advice on organizing and formatting a comment letter so it is clear and persuasive to the agency reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Things to consider about a regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some things to consider about a regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages commenters to analyze substantive aspects of the proposed regulation (e.g., impacts, assumptions, costs, benefits) when crafting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing the legality of a regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the legality of a regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on evaluating legal issues with a proposed rule—whether the agency has authority, statutory requirements, and potential legal vulnerabilities to raise in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics of commenting on the rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanics of commenting on the rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practical steps for submitting comments (deadlines, docket procedures, where/how to file) so comments are timely and properly filed with the agency.
